title: pkg/binfmt.MaybeRegister(): don't assume we have a useful binfmt_misc fs, use gas more
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

Don't assume that, if emulation is available, its status can be determined by walking entries under `/proc/sys/fs/binfmt_misc`, which may not be mounted in the namespace where we're running.

Instead, try running some trivial example binaries for a few architectures, and if they don't fail due to executable formats being wrong, just assume that whatever we need will be available, and leave things be.
To keep the binaries small, they were (and will be, if need be at build-time) built using gas from GNU binutils rather than Go's built-in assembler.
Because their function (print "OK" and exit) is pretty similar to what the entrypoint binary we embed in confidential workload images does, we also now have binutils-built versions of that for a few more architectures, should we need them.

Check a $BUILDAH_REGISTER_BINFMT environment variable to force whether or not we do anything here.

#### How to verify it

New unit test!

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #6611

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

```release-note
`buildah run` and `buildah build` are now more cautious about registering configured emulators when running inside of containers, and that behavior can be forced one way or the other using the BUILDAH_REGISTER_BINFMT environment variable.
```
